item.title: Grace Khelan and Thaddeus Kwong return to the pool tonight at Youth Olympics
item.description: Team Fiji swimmers, Grace Khelan and Thaddeus Kwong will be taking to the pool tonight at the Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal. Khelan will be participating in the 50 metres Freestyle heats at 10pm, before also swimming in the Women's 50 metres Butterfly heats at 11pm.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji swimmers, Grace Khelan and Thaddeus Kwong will be taking to the pool tonight at the Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal.

Khelan will be participating in the 50 metres Freestyle heats at 10pm, before also swimming in the Women's 50 metres Butterfly heats at 11pm.

Kwong will be participating in the Men's 50 metres Butterfly heats at 11.11pm.

Last night, Kwong swam a new personal best of 1 minute 0.66 seconds in the Men’s 100m Backstroke, finishing 14th of 29.

Also last night, our futsal girls went down 5–1 to Ukraine in their Group A match.

item.title: Kadavu hooker selected for Fijian Latui team to play Munster and Ireland A

item.content:encoded:
26-year-old Joseva Baleloa, a hooker for the Kadavu Rugby Union, could not hold back his tears and emotions when he was announced as part of the Fijian Latui team that will play a Munster Selection and Ireland A.

Baleloa says his thoughts immediately turned to his father, who has struggled but continued to support him throughout his rugby journey, never giving up on him even during difficult times.

The Nakaseleka, Kadavu hooker previously played for Naitasiri and Namosi before returning to represent his vanua, Kadavu, where he earned his call-up to the Fijian Latui squad.

The former Queen Victoria School and Marist Brothers High School student became emotional while speaking to fijivillage Sports, saying the sacrifices he had made and the long wait had finally been worth it.

The Fijian Latui squad announced today includes 10 locally based players, with the remainder made up of overseas-based players.

Former Fiji 7s player Kaminieli Rasuka and Mesake Doge were among the notable names included in the squad announced today.

The Latui will play Munster Selection next Saturday, before meeting Ireland A on 20th November.

item.title: Naitasiri focused on rebuilding confidence ahead of Farebrother defence against Ra
item.description: Naitasiri Head Coach Timoci Tinaviti says rebuilding his players confidence is a priority as the side prepares for its first Inkk Farebrother Trophy defence against Vodafone Vanua champions Ra this Saturday. Tinaviti says the team understands the importance of the challenge and is expecting a tough battle against Ra.
item.content:encoded:
Naitasiri Head Coach Timoci Tinaviti says rebuilding his players confidence is a priority as the side prepares for its first Inkk Farebrother Trophy defence against Vodafone Vanua champions Ra this Saturday.

Tinaviti says the team understands the importance of the challenge and is expecting a tough battle against Ra.

He says although Naitasiri missed out on a place in the Skipper Cup final, the players are determined to put that disappointment behind them and regain the confidence of their supporters.

Tinaviti says the Farebrother Challenge is a different competition, and the team must be well prepared if they are to successfully defend the trophy.

He also highlights the strong relationship between Naitasiri and Ra, saying the upcoming clash holds significance for both sides.

Tinaviti says the players are working hard in preparation and are focused on retaining the prestigious trophy.

Naitasiri will face Ra at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori this Saturday with kick-off scheduled for 3pm.

The Farebrother Challenge will continue on 14th November when the trophy holders face Nadroga.

The holders will then take on Tailevu on 21st November before the scheduled challenge matches conclude against Nadi on 28th November.

Venues and kick-off times for the remaining challenges are yet to be confirmed.

item.title: Point Of Law wins Melbourne Cup 2026
item.description: Melbourne Cup favourite Point of Law, formerly owned by King Charles, has won the 2026 Melbourne Cup, taking home AUD$10.2 million in prize money. The British horse was ridden by Ethan Brown.
item.content:encoded:
Melbourne Cup favourite Point of Law, formerly owned by King Charles, has won the 2026 Melbourne Cup, taking home AUD$10.2 million in prize money.

The British horse was ridden by Ethan Brown.

Zahrann has finished second and Juja Kibo third.

Winning jockey, Brown says it is every jockey's dream to do this, as he cannot still believe the win.

Trainer Ciaron Maher started seven of the 23 runners and he has trained the Melbourne Cup trifecta with Point of Law, Zahrann, and Juja Kibo

Royal Supremacy who had led for most of the race was pipped by Point Of Law at the tape.
